$comment: Labels the triage agent may apply. These are AL-Go's EXISTING labels, reused deliberately rather than replaced with a parallel taxonomy - the repo already has a triage vocabulary that maintainers and reporters understand. Colour and description match what is on the repository today, so Sync-TriageLabels.ps1 reports them unchanged rather than overwriting them. That script only creates anything when passed -Create.

labels.name: Unrelated to AL-Go
labels.description: This issue is unrelated to AL-Go
labels.usedFor: recommended_lane = route-to-other-component. The comment names which component; the label just flags it.

labels.name: Need more info
labels.description: Please add more info about how to repro the problem

$notApplied.$comment: Deliberately NOT turned into labels. The information still reaches maintainers through the comment and the findings artifact.
$notApplied.fix_risk: Publishing 'this touches critical shared code' on a public issue is an unnecessary signal to anyone looking for a soft spot. Risk belongs in the artifact and in notes_for_maintainer.
$notApplied.area: 'Unrelated to AL-Go' plus a comment naming the component conveys the same thing without adding six labels to a repo that already has a working vocabulary.
$notApplied.Cannot repro: Too strong a claim for an automated first pass. A failed automated reproduction is not the same as maintainers being unable to reproduce, and conflating them would mislead.
$notApplied.maintainer workflow state: Fix Ready, In Preview, Shipped, accepted, In Progress and Under Investigation track maintainer workflow. Only a human should set them.
